answer: Sybil resistance comes from requiring each identity—whether named jade, saffron, or nebula—to complete a prescribed chain of modular squarings before it can act. In a Wesolowski VDF, each squaring depends on the previous result, so GPUs cannot parallelize a single chain to erase its elapsed-time cost. Separate clones can run on separate hardware, but each needs its own computation; the delay and resource cost make mass identity creation harder, while the proof is verified efficiently.
